description: Block-bootstrap-by-country 95% confidence intervals for the false-positive panel headline metrics. Countries are the resampling unit (each country-year's cell is within-country), so the CIs respect serial correlation and test whether lift>1 and noise-to-signal<1 survive sampling uncertainty.
verdict: Block-bootstrap-by-country (113 countries, B=5000). Under the primary spec (ratio>1, k=2y, LV_30_10): lift point 1.877 CI [1.594, 2.193] (excludes 1) and noise-to-signal point 0.461 CI [0.375, 0.569] (excludes 1). False-alarm share CI [0.698, 0.796] stays high. So the 'genuine-but-weak, false-alarm-dominated' reading is statistically supported — the signal beats chance but remains a noisy single-threshold indicator.
honest_limits: Percentile bootstrap (no bias correction); the country block ignores any cross-country contagion in the SAME crisis (e.g. 1997-98 Asia, 1980s Latin America), which would make true CIs a little wider. Same data caveats as false_positive_panel.py (WDI/DRS != BIS; mechanical crash rules, not the L&V list).
